Welcome to Caversham Primary School. This week's Right of the Week is Article 2 - You have the right to access your rights without discrimination.
Welcome to Caversham Primary School
A very warm welcome awaits you at Caversham Primary School. The school’s motto ‘Learning for Life’ is at the heart of all that we do and is lived and breathed by the whole school community each and every day. This enthusiasm for learning makes our school a very special place to come to work and learn.
What is special about us?
We are passionate about providing the best possible learning experiences for the whole child, ensuring a high quality education in its widest sense. Our carefully planned curriculum, and wealth of additional opportunities, ensures that our children are motivated by and engaged in their learning. It is this enthusiasm, from both staff and pupils, that creates the buzz that is felt in every classroom every day.
We are a Therapeutic Thinking school. Our behaviour approach and curriculum is centred around inclusivity, diversity and restorative thinking.

Rights Respecting School
Caversham Primary School is a Unicef Gold Rights Respecting School!
What is a Rights Respecting School?
UNICEF is the world’s leading organisation working for children and their rights. The Rights Respecting Schools Award is granted to schools that show commitment to promoting and realising children’s rights and encouraging adults, children and young people to respect the rights of others in school. Gold is the highest accolade given by UNICEF UK and shows a deep and thorough commitment to children’s rights at all levels of school life. There are over 600 schools across England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales that have received Gold.
The Award recognises achievement in putting the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child at the heart of a school’s planning, policies and practice. A Rights Respecting School is a community where children’s rights are learned, taught, practised, respected, protected and promoted.
The UNICEF UK Rights Respecting Schools initiative is aimed at schools across the UK, including those in an early years setting. Currently, it works with nearly 5,000 primary schools, secondary schools, schools for children and young people with special educational needs and pupil referral units across England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. Schools have reported a positive impact on pupil behaviour, relationships and well-being by enhancing pupils’ self-esteem, leading to less truancy and bullying, better learning and improved academic standards.
Have a look at the amazing work that our pupils have produced as part of being a Rights Respecting School...

pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
The Extended School Clubs are run by members of the Caversham Primary Staff and offer wrap-around childcare for children attending the school.
Breakfast Club runs from 08:00 until the start of school when children are taken to their classrooms. As the name suggests, breakfast is provided within this time.
Breakfast Club costs £5.00 (rising to £5.50 on 01/09/2026) per session.
After School Club runs from the end of the school day until 18:00. Children are given a cold light supper and, weather permitting, spend much of the time playing outside.
After School Club costs £15.00 (rising to £16.50 on 01/09/2026) per session.
The clubs are extremely popular, so if you wish to register your child/children please download and complete the relevant application form below and return to the school office or e-mail to extendedschools@cavershamprimary.reading.sch.uk. Once the form is received, you will be contacted via email and advised of the availability at that time.
Payment can be made via bank transfer, Childcare Vouchers or Tax Free Childcare vouchers.
For all Breakfast & After School Club queries, please contact Mrs Musselwhite below:
extendedschools@cavershamprimary.reading.sch.uk

Extra-curricular Clubs
We are proud of the wide range of extra- curricular clubs that are offered at Caversham Primary School.
We work with a number of outside providers to run extra- curricular clubs before and after school as well as offering teacher- led clubs before, during and at the end of the school day.
Our extra- curricular clubs offer changes each term so that we are able to provide opportunities to as many of our pupils as possible.
Please see below for our latest clubs timetable.
SCHOOL CLUBS LIST - Jan 26

SEND
Our SENCO is Ms. Sutton who is responsible for advocating for the needs of all of our pupils who have special education needs and disabilities (SEND). As a school, we are passionate about supporting every child to thrive. If you would like to speak to Ms. Sutton about your child you can contact her here: senco@cavershamprimary.reading.sch.uk
